rv.q: But, although Marianne Elliott's production has its moments, it never quite achieves the painful delirium of classic Ayckbourn revivals.
Painfully funny and piercingly desolate, it’s a side-aching, heartbreaking depiction of loneliness, self-delusion and misery in middle-class suburbia.
No, this old writing, painfully arthritic, stale and politically inert.

cn.t: Ayckbourn's festive family comedy gets a star-studded revival that never quite reaches the painful delirium of classic productions, despite strong casting including Catherine Tate and Mark Gatiss.
